request.spec:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias (as names are
compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge
does (claims after theirs, aliases joined, bound figures lost); the other sheet writes
PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> from=<sheet id> then PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>.

agent.result_text:
A transfer now merges the arriving person into someone already on the other sheet who has their name or one of their aliases, instead of refusing. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What happens on a merge:**
- The arriving person's claims go after the existing person's. Numbered claims take the other sheet's next numbers, and figures a statement had bound are lost.
- Their name and aliases become aliases of the existing person. In the test, Ada's aliases end up as "Ad, Addie, addie".
- The other sheet's audit gets `PERSON_TRANSFERRED … name=<name> from=<sheet>`, then `PERSON_MERGED … from=<name> into=<name>`, then the usual rollup lines. The leaving sheet's audit lines are unchanged.

**Things that behave differently from what you might assume:**
- **Aliases no longer have to be unique on a sheet.** The database blocked two aliases that differ only in case, but the expected result needs both "Addie" and "addie" on Ada. A new migration, `V63__person_alias_shared.sql`, makes that index non-unique. The app still refuses adding an alias that is already taken, so this only affects merges.
- **Contacts:** when the person merges, their contact is dropped (as in a normal merge), so a contact already on the other sheet doesn't block it. A plain transfer still refuses a clashing contact.
- **Still refused:** a name used on another sheet of the target's tree; a name and alias that match two different people on the other sheet; or a match who is retired. The test doesn't cover any of these.

The main change is in `TransferPerson.java`, with small edits to `Transferred.java`, `AuditPersonTransferred.java` and the comment in `transfer.POST.yml`. The front end needed no changes.
